description: 1. The agent must read SKILL.md to learn about Basic Memory's Task schema system. It must first write a complete schema note to `memory/schema/Task.md` with `type: schema`, `entity: Task`, `version: 1`, and a full `schema:` block including status, steps, current_step, blockers, context, etc. — replacing the stub file left there. 2. For each of the three work briefs in `pipeline/stages/`, the agent must call `write_note(note_type='Task', ...)` with: (a) a `metadata` dict containing `status`, `steps` (list), `current_step` (integer), and other relevant fields; and (b) a content body that includes BOTH observation-style lines (`- [status] active`, `- [description] ...`, `- [current_step] 1`) AND markdown sections `## Steps` with numbered checkboxes (`1. [ ] Step text`) and `## Context`. This dual-representation is the key proprietary trap — a naive agent will omit one side. 3. The crystallography task must be written with `status: 'blocked'` and a non-empty `blockers` array in its frontmatter metadata (CPD-001 resupply + soaking conditions). 4. The agent must call `schema_validate(noteType='Task')` (capital T in the argument) to validate all tasks. 5. The critical trap: when searching, the agent must use lowercase `note_types=['task']` not `note_types=['Task']`, because `write_note(note_type='Task')` stores the type as lowercase `task` in frontmatter.
